paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nothing is too difficult for the LORD, and that includes keeping a promise when everything around it looks lost. Jeremiah prays, "Nothing is too difficult for You!" (Jeremiah 32:17). Then God asks him right back, "Is anything too difficult for Me?" (Jeremiah 32:27). Both of them are saying the same thing, and I'd say it's worth saying twice.

The passage doesn't pretend the hard part away, though. God says plainly that His people turned their backs to Him and not their faces, and that He taught them again and again while they would not listen (Jeremiah 32:33). The city would fall, just as He had said. But the story doesn't stop at the disaster, because God says, "I will surely gather My people from all the lands to which I have banished them…" (Jeremiah 32:37). He also promises, "I will never turn away from doing good to them…" (Jeremiah 32:40). So when you read about what people did, and then read what God does next, that second part is the one to hold onto.

So what does that mean for you, baker? God's promises don't depend on how things look today. Fields would be bought again, deeds signed, sealed and witnessed, "because I will restore them from captivity, declares the LORD" (Jeremiah 32:44). When your own situation looks like a dead end, remember that God can do what looks impossible, and He keeps His word. I was sitting in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and the God who made everything reached in and brought me out. Trust Him with what looks too hard, because it isn't too hard for Him.
